column1: # ZAP alert gating rules — OWASP's own convention (from zap-baseline.py/
# zap-full-scan.py), reused here for run-and-gate.ts's gate.
# Format: <ruleId>\t<IGNORE|WARN|FAIL>\t(comment)[\t<site>[\t<confidence>]]
# - ruleId is ZAP's numeric plugin ID (https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/)
# - site, optional, is a site name exactly as the report gives it, such as
#   http://localhost:3000: the rule then applies to that site only. Leave it
#   empty to give a confidence for every site.
# - confidence, optional, is one of ZAP's confidence levels: Low, Medium, High
#   or Confirmed. The rule then applies to alerts at that confidence only, so
#   an IGNORE for a Low-confidence false positive still fails the same plugin
#   at a higher confidence. Any other value stops the gate.
# - When several rules match an alert, the one that names the most wins: site
#   and confidence, then site, then confidence, then neither.
# - IGNORE: triaged as a known false positive — stays visible in the report
#   (same as WARN) and does not fail the build; the difference from WARN is
#   documentation only, marking that someone has already looked at it
# - WARN: visible in the report, does not fail the build, not yet triaged
# - FAIL: fails the build
# Unlisted rules default to: FAIL if High risk, WARN otherwise — see
# utils/zap/gate.ts.
